references.text: Fear and dread fell upon the peoples when Israel came out of Egypt, which Rahab refers to when she says that the inhabitants of the land are seized with fear.
God promised to send terror before Israel to drive out the peoples of Canaan, as Rahab confirms has happened.
Moses' words that God would put fear and dread of Israel upon all peoples under heaven are confirmed by Rahab's testimony.
The promise that no one could stand against Israel and that fear and dread would come upon the peoples is fulfilled in what Rahab recounts.
It confirms Rahab's words by telling how the kings of the land lost heart when they heard about Israel's crossing of the Jordan.
God gives Jericho into Joshua's hand, as fulfillment of what Rahab acknowledged—that the Lord had given them the land.
Hebrews mentions Rahab's faith as the reason she did not perish with the unbelievers, based on her confession in this verse.
